questions.question: Name and locate the three main areas of tropical rainforest in the world.
questions.expected_answer: The largest is the Amazon rainforest in South America, mostly in Brazil but also in countries such as Peru and Colombia. The second is the Congo Basin rainforest in central Africa, in countries such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon and Cameroon. The third is in Southeast Asia, on islands such as Borneo, Sumatra and New Guinea. All are near the equator, between the tropics.

questions.question: Describe the climate of a tropical rainforest.
questions.expected_answer: The climate is hot all year, with average temperatures of about twenty-five to twenty-eight degrees and a very small annual range of one to three degrees. It is very wet, usually with more than two thousand millimetres of rain a year and rain in every month. The air is very humid. Each day, the sun heats the ground, warm, moist air rises and forms thunderclouds, and convectional rain falls in the afternoon.

questions.question: Explain how a rainforest climate graph differs from a climate graph for Pietermaritzburg.
questions.expected_answer: A rainforest climate graph has an almost flat temperature line, close to twenty-six or twenty-seven degrees all year, and tall rainfall bars in every month with no dry month. A climate graph for Pietermaritzburg has a temperature line that rises in summer and falls in winter, with a larger range of about eight to ten degrees, and rainfall bars that are tall in summer but very short in winter.
